name: Slovakia: participant-facing document QC
item_format: Each result records the item id, the outcome, a short rationale and evidence (quoted passage and source locator) or an explicit gap.

items.check: Full and short trial title are the same as in the protocol and in every other document.
Protocol number and current version match the protocol.
Sponsor name matches the protocol and CTIS.
EU trial number is given where available.
Investigational treatment and comparator are described as in the protocol and IB/SmPC.
Visit duration and overall participation period match the protocol.
Contact details and site information are current and complete.
No internal drafting notes, tracked changes, unresolved placeholders or references to another country remain.

sections.title: Protocol-to-participant consistency
sections.instruction: Check the Slovak text against the protocol schedule and safety sections.

items.check: Screening tests, randomisation, blinding, treatment periods and washouts are described at the correct level.
Invasive procedures, imaging, sampling and genetic testing are described at the correct level.
Questionnaires and long-term follow-up are described at the correct level.
Contraception, pregnancy testing and prohibited medicines match the protocol.
Standard care and research-only procedures are distinguished.
No promise of results, treatment access or medical benefit that the protocol does not provide.
Planned remote contacts, electronic consent or other decentralised elements are explained.
Main-trial consent is not bundled with optional future research, recordings, genetic analysis or other substudies.
Each optional choice allows a clear yes or no without affecting main-trial eligibility, unless the activity is scientifically required by the protocol (then explained and not labelled optional).
The form states that participation is voluntary, questions are allowed, refusal does not affect care, and consent may be withdrawn.
Withdrawal is explained separately for treatment, safety follow-up, data already collected and remaining samples.
The standard signature block lets the participant and the person conducting the consent discussion sign and personally date the form.
Legal-representative, witness or parent blocks appear only in the document pathway where they apply.

The consent section confirms in separate statements: information received and understood; enough time and opportunity to ask questions; voluntariness; agreement to the main trial procedures; permitted source-record access; information on privacy, injury, reimbursement and withdrawal; separate optional choices.
The person signing has legal authority for the decision (parent or legal representative recognised under Slovak law, verified).
Re-consent is planned for new safety information that could affect willingness to continue, reaching 18 and regained capacity.
Every protocol population maps to an approved information and consent route (population × document table; every inclusion pathway has a document set).
Healthy volunteers: explicit no-direct-benefit and payment explanation; separate documents if patients are also enrolled.
Minors: parent or legal-representative permission and age-appropriate information for each planned band; assent and dissent handling; re-consent at 18.
Adults unable to consent: legal-representative route and participant involvement (adapted information or assent, objection respected).
Emergency enrolment: Article 35 pathway and subsequent consent documents for participant and legal representative.
Participants or representatives unable to read: impartial-witness procedure; oral-consent record with witness signature when the person cannot write.
Pregnancy follow-up: correct form for the pregnant participant or the pregnant partner.
Optional future data or sample use has a separate choice.
No consent pathway for people in custody, serving a prison sentence or held in detention (prohibited by Slovak law).
All participant text is in natural Slovak understandable by the intended population.
Abbreviations are expanded at first use.
Literal translations that do not match Slovak clinical or regulatory usage are replaced.
Defined trial terms are consistent across all documents.
The Slovak text was compared sentence by sentence with the English source.
items.applies_when: an English source or master exists

items.check: Numbers, units, dates, probabilities, treatment names, visit frequencies, sample volumes, contraception periods and contact details are verified.
Formatting does not hide qualifications or make optional text look mandatory.
The privacy section identifies controllers, processing purposes, data categories, recipients, source-record access, international transfers, retention, participant rights and the complaint route.
Consistent with the GDPR statement submitted in CTIS (SK-R1) and with sponsor and site privacy responsibilities.
Does not say that all data can be deleted after withdrawal; explains which records may need to be retained for trial integrity and legal obligations.
Consent to the clinical trial is not used as a blanket GDPR consent for every processing activity.
Access by monitors, auditors and authorities is explained without suggesting that confidentiality is absolute.
The main-trial sample description matches the protocol and laboratory manual.
Collection, purpose, coding, analysis location, transfers, storage period, destruction and withdrawal handling are stated.
Optional future use is distinguishable from required trial testing.
The scope of future use is defined without unlimited phrases such as 'any research forever'.
Genetic analysis is stated directly, with whether individual results will be returned.
Consistent with the S1 biological-samples form (SK-S1).
The Slovak version is the participant-use version.
English and Slovak versions align where both are submitted.
The current national Ethics Committee contact route, including the required telephone details, appears in the Participant Information Sheet (recurring ŠÚKL 2025 deficiency).
Travel and other expense reimbursement is explained, including conditions and what happens after withdrawal (recurring ŠÚKL 2025 deficiency).
Injury and insurance wording matches the valid Slovakia certificate (SK-O1).
The version 2.0 recruitment and consent procedure template is used for submissions from 1 September 2026 and K1 matches the document pathways.
Only documents permitted by the Clinical Trials Regulation and the current Commission Q&A are uploaded.
The CTIS documents are blank and contain no participant personal data.
Version number, date, language, population and country are in the filename and footer.
The participant-use form is signed only when consent is obtained; the approved signature blocks match the planned process.
The participant receives a signed copy.
Evidence of translation review and approval is retained in the trial file.
No drafting instruction remains in the final version ([bracket] notes, italic notes, '...........' gaps, yellow form labels).
Every final PDF opened after conversion: page order, bookmarks if used, line breaks and special Slovak characters correct.
Signature fields present; text selectable; no comments or hidden content.
Each file goes to the correct CTIS placeholder with the required publication or personal-data handling.
The document inventory is reconciled with the Slovakia Part II document checklist.
